summary: Establishes an IETF URN sub-namespace for use with OAuth-related specifications. This gives them a place for stable, unique names. It is informational and not an Internet Standards Track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC creates an IETF URN sub-namespace for OAuth-related specifications. It also describes how a new OAuth URN can be requested and registered.

questions: where do oauth urns come from
how to register an oauth urn
what is the oauth uri registry
subtitle: A registered URN sub-namespace for OAuth-related specifications and parameters.

tldr.problem: OAuth extensions and companion specifications need URIs to identify functionality and related context.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC establishes urn:ietf:params:oauth and a registration template with a Specification Required procedure.
tldr.outcome: IANA registers the sub-namespace and an OAuth URI registry for values beneath it.

today: RFC 6755 is an Informational document, and the unit metadata lists no update or replacement. It establishes the OAuth URN sub-namespace and its registration procedure.

sections.title: A URN Namespace for OAuth
sections.content:
OAuth extensions and companion specifications may use Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) to identify an extension or related context. RFC 6755 creates and registers the sub-namespace urn:ietf:params:oauth for these uses.

The RFC says OAuth-related parameters can be established beneath this sub-namespace.
sections.plainLanguage: OAuth-related specifications get a shared place to create identifying names. Each name can identify a feature or concept related to OAuth.

sections.title: How to Request a New URN
sections.content:
A request uses the form urn:ietf:params:oauth:<value>, where the value represents the functionality or concept being registered. New entries use the Specification Required procedure described in RFC 5226.

The request template asks for the URN, its common name, the change controller, and the document that specifies it. For Standards Track RFCs, the change controller is listed as IETF; for other requests, the responsible party is named.
sections.plainLanguage: A registration request names the function, gives it a common name, identifies who controls changes, and points to its specification.

sections.title: Example Registration Request
sections.content:
The RFC provides an example for a new OAuth 2.0 grant type. Its sample URN is urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:example, and the common name is "An Example Grant Type for OAuth 2.0".

For the part after the namespace, the RFC suggests including a class and an identifier within that class, separated by a colon. Other arrangements may also be used.
sections.plainLanguage: The example uses a grant-type class followed by an example identifier. The RFC suggests this structure but allows other value formats.

sections.title: IANA Registration and Security
sections.content:
IANA registered the sub-namespace urn:ietf:params:oauth and created an "OAuth URI" registry beneath a top-level "OAuth Parameters" registry. Entries use the value after the sub-namespace as their index.

The RFC adds no security considerations beyond those inherent to URNs. It advises people working on OAuth to be familiar with the security considerations of the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA maintains a registry for OAuth URNs under the new sub-namespace. The memo adds no security concerns beyond those that apply to URNs generally.
